newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Saga quits Indonesian business.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Saga quits Indonesian business.

text.p: Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA announced on Friday it was terminating its business in Indonesia because it found it difficult to operate in a cost-effective way in the Asian country.
The oil company said it had invested 400 million crowns in Indonesia and that it was now selling its stakes there.
"Saga Petroleum will pull out of Indonesia to prioritise its international activities in other areas," a statement to the Oslo Bourse said.

"Saga has weighed a series of business opportunities in the country, but has not found a basis for increasing its investments. The company finds it difficult to operate in a cost-effective manner in Indonesia given the limited scope of its activity there," the statement said.
